To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have introduced a new method for continual learning, called NCL, which outperforms existing methods in feedforward and RNNs, and which results in the emergence of task-specific dynamics in the trained networks, similar to experimental results in biology.

we introduce a new method, Natural Continual Learning, for continual learning that outperforms existing approaches, and that it is capable of inducing task-specific dynamics in recurrent neural networks.

(i) Bayesian weight regularisation and projected gradient descent can be combined to improve continual learning performance and that (ii) the resulting network dynamics evolve task-specific properties that are preserved as new tasks emerge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: can we learn to learn? And we believe that the answer is yes.
the development of a new approach to continual learning that is inspired by natural systems, and which is able to preserve the dynamics that support previous tasks while learning new ones.

the development of new methods that can be applied in the context of continual learning, and that can be used in the future to study how biological neural networks learn multiple tasks and behaviors over the course of a life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NCL is a new approach that unifies weight regularizers and projected gradient descent to improve the performance of artificial agents in continual learning scenarios.
NCL is a simple yet powerful method to learn new tasks without forgetting old ones in feed-forward and recurrent neural networks.
our method outperforms previous methods and that it is the first method that can preserve neural dynamics in a way that is similar to biological circuits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NCL is a simple and efficient method that allows artificial agents to learn many tasks over the course (lifetime) of their lives, while maintaining performance on all of them.
NCL is a simple and effective method for continual learning that is inspired by biological learning mechanisms.
we are proposing a method that is inspired from the biological brain to address the catastrophic forgetting problem in neural networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the journey matters, as much as the destination.
continual learning can be seen as a journey through parameter space that should be guided by a suitable prior.
a single method that combines the best of both worlds, weight regularization and projected gradients, can lead to better continual learning performance than either method alone.
